sentence: Daniel says that ___ is ready.
setupText: Daniel says, 'I am ready.' Choose the report about Daniel, not about yourself.
taskText: Daniel says that ___ is ready.
text: Daniel says, 'I am ready.' Choose the report about Daniel, not about yourself. Daniel says that ___ is ready.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3241:Speaker I becomes third-person subject in a present report
explanation: He refers to Daniel as the person who is ready.

rationales.I: I would refer to the person reporting the message, but Daniel is talking about himself.
rationales.he: He refers to Daniel as the person who is ready.
rationales.him: Him is an object form; the person before is needs a subject form.
rationales.his: His shows possession and cannot stand as the subject meaning Daniel here.

sentence: She says that ___.
setupText: The cashier tells me, 'You are early.' Choose my report of her message.
taskText: She says that ___.
text: The cashier tells me, 'You are early.' Choose my report of her message. She says that ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3242:Listener you becomes I when the listener reports
explanation: The cashier's you refers to the person reporting, so my report uses I am.

rationales.she is early: She would make the cashier the early person, but her you refers to me.
rationales.they are early: They introduces other people whom the cashier did not mention.
rationales.I am early: The cashier's you refers to the person reporting, so my report uses I am.
rationales.we are early: We adds the cashier or other people to the early group; the message addresses only me.

sentence: My neighbors say that ___ live nearby.
setupText: My two neighbors say, 'We live nearby.' I am not part of their household.
taskText: My neighbors say that ___ live nearby.
text: My two neighbors say, 'We live nearby.' I am not part of their household. My neighbors say that ___ live nearby.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3243:Exclusive we reported as they
explanation: They refers to both neighbors without including the reporter.

rationales.we: We would include me, but the neighbors are speaking about their own household.
rationales.he: He refers to one man and does not keep the two neighbors together.
rationales.she: She refers to one woman, not the two people who spoke.
rationales.they: They refers to both neighbors without including the reporter.

sentence: My brother says that ___ bike is outside.
setupText: My brother says, 'My bike is outside.' Choose the report keeping the bike as his.
taskText: My brother says that ___ bike is outside.
text: My brother says, 'My bike is outside.' Choose the report keeping the bike as his. My brother says that ___ bike is outside.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3244:Possessive my adjusted for a male speaker reported by someone else
explanation: His keeps the bike as the brother's possession when I report his words.

rationales.his: His keeps the bike as the brother's possession when I report his words.
rationales.my: My would make the bike mine rather than my brother's.
rationales.her: Her assigns the bike to a woman who is not the stated owner.
rationales.our: Our would make the bike a shared possession, which the message does not say.

sentence: The customer says, 'I don't eat meat.'
setupText: Choose the report with the same meaning as the customer's words.
taskText: The customer says, 'I don't eat meat.'
text: Choose the report with the same meaning as the customer's words. The customer says, 'I don't eat meat.'
options: The customer says she eats meat.
The customer says she doesn't eat meat.
The customer says she doesn't like cooking meat.
The customer says she only eats meat.
answer: The customer says she doesn't eat meat.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3245:Negative meaning preserved in a third-person present report
explanation: Doesn't eat meat keeps the negative meaning and agrees with she.

This removes don't and reverses the customer's message.
Doesn't eat meat keeps the negative meaning and agrees with she.
rationales.The customer says she doesn't like cooki: Not liking cooking is different from not eating meat.
Only eats meat says meat is her only food, almost the opposite of the source.

sentence: The driver ___ me that this is the last stop.
setupText: Choose the verb that fits directly before 'me' in this sentence.
taskText: The driver ___ me that this is the last stop.
text: Choose the verb that fits directly before 'me' in this sentence. The driver ___ me that this is the last stop.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3246:Tell with a direct listener object
explanation: 'Tell' can take the listener directly: 'tells me that this is the last stop'.

rationales.says: 'Say' needs 'to' before a listener: 'says to me', not 'says me'.
rationales.speaks: 'Speaks' does not take 'me' directly before a that clause in this pattern.
rationales.tells: 'Tell' can take the listener directly: 'tells me that this is the last stop'.
rationales.talks: 'Talk' normally uses a preposition for the listener, such as 'talks to me', not 'talks me that'.

sentence: The host said ___ the guest that dinner was ready.
setupText: Complete the report using 'said' and the listener correctly.
taskText: The host said ___ the guest that dinner was ready.
text: Complete the report using 'said' and the listener correctly. The host said ___ the guest that dinner was ready.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3247:Listener introduced by to after said
explanation: 'Said to the guest' identifies the person who heard the host's message.

rationales.at: 'At' does not introduce the listener after 'said' in this reporting pattern.
rationales.for: 'For' can suggest speaking on someone's behalf, not saying these words to that person.
rationales.with: 'With' does not mark the person receiving the message after 'said'.
rationales.to: 'Said to the guest' identifies the person who heard the host's message.

sentence: The assistant says that the shop ___ open.
setupText: The assistant says, 'The shop is open.' Complete the present report.
taskText: The assistant says that the shop ___ open.
text: The assistant says, 'The shop is open.' Complete the present report. The assistant says that the shop ___ open.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3248:Present singular be inside a says-that clause
explanation: Is agrees with the singular subject the shop in the reported statement.

rationales.is: Is agrees with the singular subject the shop in the reported statement.
rationales.are: Are does not agree with the singular shop.
rationales.am: Am is used with I, not with the shop.
rationales.be: Be is the base form; this present statement needs the finite form is.

sentence: The receptionist says that the hotel is full tonight.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the hotel's message.
taskText: The receptionist says that the hotel is full tonight.
text: Choose the meaning of the hotel's message. The receptionist says that the hotel is full tonight.
options: There are many rooms to choose from tonight.
The hotel does not serve dinner tonight.
The hotel has no guests tonight.
There are no rooms available tonight.
answer: There are no rooms available tonight.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3249:Understanding the content of a simple practical report
explanation: A full hotel has no rooms available for new guests for the stated night.

rationales.There are many rooms to choose from toni: Full means there are no available rooms, not many choices.
A full hotel has no rooms available for new guests for the stated night.
The message concerns room availability, not food service.
No guests would mean the hotel was empty, the opposite of full.

sentence: The sign ___, 'Please use the other door.'
setupText: Choose the ordinary verb used to report the words on a sign.
taskText: The sign ___, 'Please use the other door.'
text: Choose the ordinary verb used to report the words on a sign. The sign ___, 'Please use the other door.'
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3250:Say used for a written source
explanation: A sign says something even though it is written rather than spoken.

rationales.tells: Tells normally needs a person here, such as tells us to use another door.
rationales.speaks: Speaks is not the ordinary verb for introducing the exact written words on a sign.
rationales.says: A sign says something even though it is written rather than spoken.
rationales.talks: Talks does not normally introduce the exact wording on a sign in this structure.

sentence: The customer asks the waiter for water, saying exactly: 'Can I have some water?'
setupText: Choose the words the customer actually says, not a report about the customer.
taskText: The customer asks the waiter for water, saying exactly: 'Can I have some water?'
text: Choose the words the customer actually says, not a report about the customer. The customer asks the waiter for water, saying exactly: 'Can I have some water?'
options: She asks if she can have water.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3251:Exact words distinguished from a summary report
explanation: This repeats the customer's own question, including I as she used it.

This describes the customer's wish but does not repeat her words.
This summarizes her request instead of quoting it.
This is a report of the question, not the exact question spoken.
rationales.Can I have some water?: This repeats the customer's own question, including I as she used it.

sentence: Yesterday, our guide ___ us a story about the village.
setupText: Choose the correct past form in this report.
taskText: Yesterday, our guide ___ us a story about the village.
text: Choose the correct past form in this report. Yesterday, our guide ___ us a story about the village.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3252:Irregular told in a report of storytelling
explanation: Told is the past form of tell and can be followed by us a story.

rationales.told: Told is the past form of tell and can be followed by us a story.
rationales.telled: The past form is irregular: told, not telled.
rationales.tell: Tell is the base form, not the past form needed for yesterday's event.
rationales.telling: Telling cannot be the finite past verb on its own here.

sentence: A: 'The cook says that lunch is ready.' B: 'The cook says lunch is ready.'
setupText: Compare these two ways to pass on the same message.
taskText: A: 'The cook says that lunch is ready.' B: 'The cook says lunch is ready.'
text: Compare these two ways to pass on the same message. A: 'The cook says that lunch is ready.' B: 'The cook says lunch is ready.'
options: Both can report the same message.
Only A can report the cook's message.
B means that the cook is ready, not lunch.
A reports a question, but B reports an answer.
answer: Both can report the same message.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3253:Optional that in a simple speech report
explanation: Both sentences say what the cook's message is; leaving out that does not change it.

That can be left out after says in this short report, so B is also possible.
Both sentences say what the cook's message is; leaving out that does not change it.
rationales.B means that the cook is ready, not lunc: Lunch remains the subject of is ready in both sentences.
rationales.A reports a question, but B reports an a: Both report a statement about lunch; that does not turn A into a question.

sentence: The barber says that he knows ___.
setupText: The barber says to me, 'I know you.' Complete my report about his words.
taskText: The barber says that he knows ___.
text: The barber says to me, 'I know you.' Complete my report about his words. The barber says that he knows ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3254:Object pronoun for the reporter as original listener
explanation: Me is the object form referring to the original listener, who is now reporting.

rationales.I: I is a subject form, but knows needs an object here.
rationales.my: My needs a following noun and cannot mean me by itself.
rationales.me: Me is the object form referring to the original listener, who is now reporting.
rationales.mine: Mine shows possession; the message is about knowing a person, not owning something.

sentence: My aunt says, 'I can drive.'
setupText: Choose the report keeping the meaning of 'can'.
taskText: My aunt says, 'I can drive.'
text: Choose the report keeping the meaning of 'can'. My aunt says, 'I can drive.'
options: My aunt says she wants to drive.
My aunt says she can drive.
My aunt says she needs to drive.
My aunt says she cannot drive.
answer: My aunt says she can drive.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3255:Ability preserved when relaying a can statement
explanation: 'Can' keeps the aunt's statement that she is able to drive.

'Want' expresses a wish, not the ability stated with 'can'.
'Need' expresses necessity, not the stated ability.
'Cannot' reverses the positive statement about driving.
'Can' keeps the aunt's statement that she is able to drive.

sentence: Our friends say that they ___ outside.
setupText: Our friends phone now: 'We are waiting outside.' Complete the report of their current activity.
taskText: Our friends say that they ___ outside.
text: Our friends phone now: 'We are waiting outside.' Complete the report of their current activity. Our friends say that they ___ outside.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3256:Present continuous retained under a present reporting verb
explanation: Are waiting agrees with they and keeps the activity in progress now.

rationales.are waiting: Are waiting agrees with they and keeps the activity in progress now.
rationales.is waiting: Is does not agree with the plural subject they.
rationales.waiting: Waiting needs are to make a complete present-continuous verb here.
rationales.are wait: After are, this ongoing activity needs the -ing form waiting.

sentence: The tourist ___, 'Where is the station?'
setupText: Choose the verb describing the tourist's words.
taskText: The tourist ___, 'Where is the station?'
text: Choose the verb describing the tourist's words. The tourist ___, 'Where is the station?'
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3257:Ask identified as the reporting verb for an information question
explanation: Asks introduces a question seeking the station's location.

rationales.answers: Answers would give information in reply; these words request information.
rationales.asks: Asks introduces a question seeking the station's location.
rationales.thanks: Thanks expresses gratitude, which this location question does not do.
rationales.agrees: Agrees expresses acceptance of another idea, not a request for directions.

sentence: The shopkeeper says, 'We close at six.'
setupText: Choose the report that keeps both the time and the meaning of the shopkeeper's words.
taskText: The shopkeeper says, 'We close at six.'
text: Choose the report that keeps both the time and the meaning of the shopkeeper's words. The shopkeeper says, 'We close at six.'
options: The shopkeeper says the shop closes at six.
The shopkeeper says the shop opens at six.
The shopkeeper says the shop closes before six.
The shopkeeper says the shop is closed all day.
answer: The shopkeeper says the shop closes at six.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3258:Practical schedule information preserved in a report
explanation: This reports the shop's closing time without changing the action or time.

rationales.The shopkeeper says the shop opens at si: Opens reverses the action described by close.
rationales.The shopkeeper says the shop closes befo: Before six moves closing earlier than the stated time.
rationales.The shopkeeper says the shop closes at s: This reports the shop's closing time without changing the action or time.
rationales.The shopkeeper says the shop is closed a: Closed all day is different from closing at six after being open.

sentence: Yesterday, the farmer ___ that the apples were ready to pick.
setupText: Choose the past reporting verb for yesterday's message.
taskText: Yesterday, the farmer ___ that the apples were ready to pick.
text: Choose the past reporting verb for yesterday's message. Yesterday, the farmer ___ that the apples were ready to pick.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3259:Past said used to locate the speech event
explanation: Said is the past form of say, matching yesterday's message.

rationales.say: Say is not the past form required for yesterday's message.
rationales.says: Says is a present form; the message is explicitly placed yesterday.
rationales.saying: Saying needs an auxiliary and cannot be the only finite verb here.
rationales.said: Said is the past form of say, matching yesterday's message.

sentence: What does the woman say about the bag?
setupText: A woman points to a bag and says, 'That is not my bag.' Choose the report keeping her meaning.
taskText: What does the woman say about the bag?
text: A woman points to a bag and says, 'That is not my bag.' Choose the report keeping her meaning. What does the woman say about the bag?
options: She says it is not her bag.
She says it is her bag.
She says she has no bag.
She says the bag is mine.
answer: She says it is not her bag.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a1-3260:A specific ownership denial preserved without broadening it
explanation: Not her bag preserves both her denial and the ownership reference in my.

Not her bag preserves both her denial and the ownership reference in my.
This removes not and changes a denial of ownership into a claim of ownership.
She denies owning this particular bag; she does not say she owns no bag at all.
The woman does not identify the reporter as the owner, so mine adds unsupported information.
